ipc_channel_type.title: IPC Channel Type
ipc_channel_type.description: The type of inter-process communication channel used between the application and filesystem proxy/daemon.

ipc_channel_encryption_enabled.title: IPC Channel Encryption Enabled
ipc_channel_encryption_enabled.description: Whether the IPC channel applies an application-layer encryption or integrity wrapper to data in transit between application and filesystem daemon.

ipc_socket_permissions_restrictive.title: IPC Socket/Pipe Permissions Restrictive
ipc_socket_permissions_restrictive.description: Whether the UNIX socket or named pipe has filesystem permissions and ownership that restrict access to only the intended communicating processes (e.g., mode 0600 or 0660 owned by a dedicated service account).

kernel_tracing_interfaces_accessible.title: Kernel Tracing Interfaces Accessible to Co-resident Processes
kernel_tracing_interfaces_accessible.description: Whether kernel tracing or /proc-based introspection interfaces (e.g., ptrace, /proc/<pid>/mem, eBPF tracing, ftrace) are accessible to unprivileged or moderately privileged co-resident processes.

integrity_verification_enabled.title: Integrity Verification on Read Path
integrity_verification_enabled.description: Whether the application performs cryptographic integrity verification (e.g., HMAC, digital signature, or hash check) on data read from the filesystem before consuming it.

filesystem_write_accessible_to_non_owner.title: Filesystem Path Writable by Non-Owner Principals
filesystem_write_accessible_to_non_owner.description: Whether the filesystem path(s) from which the application reads sensitive data are writable by principals other than the owning application account.

read_path_on_shared_or_network_filesyste.title: Read Path Located on Shared or Network Filesystem
read_path_on_shared_or_network_filesyste.description: Whether the filesystem path(s) read by the application reside on a shared or network-mounted filesystem (e.g., NFS, SMB/CIFS, FUSE, shared tmpfs), increasing the attack surface for tampering.

shm_owner_isolation_enforced.title: Shared Memory Owner Isolation Enforced
shm_owner_isolation_enforced.description: Whether access to the shared memory segment is restricted to the owning user/group only (permissions 0600 or 0660 at most, no world bits). True means isolation is enforced; false means broader access is permitted.

shm_world_readable.title: Shared Memory Segment World-Readable
shm_world_readable.description: Whether the shared memory segment or mmap file is readable by any user on the system (world-readable bit set). True indicates any local process can attach and read data in transit.

shm_segment_permissions.title: Shared Memory Segment Permissions
shm_segment_permissions.description: The octal permission mask applied to the shared memory segment or mmap-backed file (e.g., '0777', '0600'). Overly permissive modes allow unprivileged processes to attach and read in-flight data.

pipe_directory_world_writable.title: Pipe Directory World-Writable
pipe_directory_world_writable.description: Indicates whether the directory containing the named pipe (FIFO) is world-writable or group-writable by untrusted users, enabling an attacker to delete and recreate the FIFO.

pipe_creation_uses_exclusive_flag.title: Named Pipe Created with Exclusive/Atomic Flag
pipe_creation_uses_exclusive_flag.description: Indicates whether the application creates the named pipe using an atomic or exclusive creation mechanism that prevents TOCTOU substitution.

pipe_ownership_verified_before_open.title: Pipe Ownership and Type Verified Before Open
pipe_ownership_verified_before_open.description: Indicates whether the consumer/reader process verifies that the filesystem object at the pipe path is owned by the expected user, is of type FIFO, and has correct permissions before opening it.

cache_side_channel_mitigation_enabled.title: Page-Cache Side-Channel Mitigation Enabled
cache_side_channel_mitigation_enabled.description: Whether the application or OS deployment has countermeasures active against kernel page-cache timing side channels (e.g., O_DIRECT, cache-partitioning, or process isolation mechanisms).

co_resident_untrusted_processes_permitte.title: Co-Resident Untrusted Processes Permitted
co_resident_untrusted_processes_permitte.description: Whether untrusted or multi-tenant processes are permitted to run on the same physical or virtual host, sharing the kernel page cache with the target application.

sensitive_file_access_pattern.title: Sensitive File Access Pattern
sensitive_file_access_pattern.description: Whether the application accesses sensitive files (e.g., secrets, key material, private data) through the kernel page cache in a timing-observable manner.

uses_abstract_socket.title: Uses Abstract Namespace Socket
uses_abstract_socket.description: Indicates whether the application communicates over a Linux abstract namespace socket. Abstract sockets are not tied to the filesystem and are accessible to any process in the same network namespace.

peer_credential_verification_enabled.title: Peer Credential Verification Enabled
peer_credential_verification_enabled.description: Indicates whether the application calls SO_PEERCRED (or equivalent) on accepted connections and validates the peer's UID/GID/PID against an allowlist before processing requests.

socket_namespace_isolation.title: Network Namespace Isolation Level
socket_namespace_isolation.description: Describes whether the abstract socket is confined to an isolated network namespace or is exposed in the host/shared network namespace accessible to untrusted processes.

filesystem_layer_type.title: Filesystem Abstraction Layer Type
filesystem_layer_type.description: The type of filesystem abstraction or caching layer in use between the application and underlying storage.

cache_freshness_validation_enabled.title: Cache Freshness Validation Enabled
cache_freshness_validation_enabled.description: Whether the filesystem abstraction layer enforces freshness tokens, ETags, sequence numbers, or equivalent mechanisms to prevent stale/replayed cache responses.

fuse_handler_integrity_verified.title: FUSE Handler Integrity Verified
fuse_handler_integrity_verified.description: Indicates whether the FUSE daemon binary and its configuration are integrity-verified (e.g., via package manager signatures, IMA/EVM, or code-signing), ensuring the handler has not been tampered with.

fuse_daemon_privilege_level.title: FUSE Daemon Privilege Level
fuse_daemon_privilege_level.description: The privilege level under which the FUSE user-space daemon runs, indicating its ability to manipulate data in transit and the impact of a compromise.

io_rate_limiting_enabled.title: I/O Rate Limiting Enabled
io_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Indicates whether the application or OS-level configuration enforces I/O rate limits or bandwidth throttling on filesystem data paths (e.g., cgroups blkio, ionice classes, application-level throttles).

io_queue_depth_limit.title: I/O Queue Depth Limit
io_queue_depth_limit.description: The maximum number of outstanding I/O operations permitted for the process or device queue. A value of 0 indicates no limit is configured.

process_io_priority_class.title: Process I/O Priority Class
process_io_priority_class.description: The I/O scheduling priority class assigned to the process. 'none' means no priority class is set, allowing the process to compete at the default best-effort level without restriction.

kernel_tracing_interfaces_enabled.title: Kernel Tracing Interfaces Enabled
kernel_tracing_interfaces_enabled.description: Indicates whether kernel-level tracing interfaces (auditd, strace, eBPF/bpftrace, ftrace) are active and capturing filesystem-related syscalls on the host.

tracing_access_control_enforced.title: Tracing Interface Access Control Enforced
tracing_access_control_enforced.description: Indicates whether access to kernel tracing outputs (audit log files, eBPF ring buffers, perf pipe outputs) is restricted to privileged users via filesystem permissions, MAC policies, or capability restrictions.

audit_log_encryption_at_rest.title: Audit Log Encryption at Rest
audit_log_encryption_at_rest.description: Indicates whether the audit trail output files or ring buffer backing storage are encrypted at rest, preventing offline extraction of captured plaintext filesystem data.
